## kb_to_source

Sentence-by-sentence read of the documents above and of the rest of the corpus:

- Every normative claim has a structured source (rule, baseline, factor ladder, compute, parameter, event meaning, or tool contract). Clarifying statements trace to compute: "A cap only lowers: the capped deductible is the lower of the option deductible and the cap" (`MN`); loyalty "never goes below zero" (`MX(0, …)`); "No fault determination on the claim → Full" (`fault_rows > 0`); "A vehicle bought new from a dealer is one whose physical damage coverage record shows no photo inspection due date" (`not F('inspection_due_date')`); prior-damage Q&A on Select Shop payments (`payee_type='insured'`); "a vehicle added with an effective date on the loss date itself is not added after it" (strict `>`).
- No added confirmation, review, notification, wait or step was found. Worked examples are labelled hypothetical and carry no task value (grep for 262.5, 31003, 5245.24, 36412, 27350, 38995, PD-2026, Fifth Third, Outback, Kowalczyk: no hit).
- Prerequisite-side check 1 (cross-problem operational guidance): none. Each of the three tool names appears only in its own hub (grep over the whole runtime KB). No "if unmet, first …" sentence.
- Prerequisite-side check 2 (opening world state written as a policy fact): none.
- Retired surface: the three retirement lists contain exactly the six clauses the overwrites declare; no clause is retired that the source did not retire; the remaining clauses of the same base policies are carried as in force.

Non-defect observations (policy-side notes; they do not change this skill's verdict):

- PN1: Total Loss Valuation Schedule says "Sales tax paid on the actual cash value, percent" and "New car replacement, maximum age of the vehicle since its first retail delivery | 24 months". Both are faithful renderings of the source `parameter_schema` meanings of `sales_tax_rate_by_state` and `new_car_replacement_max_age_months`, while the extended rules tax "the adjusted value" and measure age "from the vehicle's addition to the auto policy". The tension is in the source's parameter meanings versus its extended rules. Here acquisition, addition and PD effective date are all 2024-09-05, so the number is unaffected.
- PN2: The retirement banner in Claims Manual: Claim Deductible Provisions says all three retired items are "superseded by the accepted-claim deductible basis now in effect". Item 3 (Deductible Rewards Step 4) is actually replaced, per the source, by the total-loss Deductible Rewards weighting (`physdmg_ext_surrender_settlement` overwrite 3). This is an imprecise description of what supersedes the clause. The retirement itself and every in-force rule are correct, so no permitted action, parameter or result changes.
- PN3: The source retires base Step 4 (credit reduces the remaining deductible) everywhere, but base `physdmg_evt_repair_payment` still says the first repair payment is "less the deductible (net of Deductible Rewards credit)". The KB renders both exactly as the source has them.

### dependency_form (revision_2)

**N1 — KB-EXPLICIT RED (new in round 2): a base document now points at a factor of this task's surrender computation.**
- Location: "Cardinal Physical Damage Coverage Claims Manual: Claim Deductible Provisions" → "Provisions no longer in force", item 3:
  > "… — no longer in force; superseded by the Deductible Rewards credit weighting now in effect for total-loss surrender settlements."
- What it states: a Deductible Rewards credit weighting exists and applies to total-loss surrender settlements. This is the factor `deductible_rewards_weighting` of `physdmg_ext_surrender_settlement`, which this task triggers: Premier, claim-free-year credit, 1.25 → credit applied 187.50.
- Why it is beyond the form: grep over the new corpus shows "weight" appears only in this sentence and in the weighting factor's own document. In revision_1 the factor's existence could be found only from the customer's records (package Cardinal Auto Premier plus a `claim_free_year` credit entry). The sentence sits in the base deductible chapter, which a solver reads when working out any claim deductible. It announces the factor before the records are consulted, and so pre-solves the factor search. The supersession relation is the source's overwrite, but the source does not require it to be stated in the base document. The replacement text itself is carried, as it should be, in the weighting document.
- Not a fix recommendation. Semantics are correct and the solution is unchanged.
- Same-kind pointers judged not RED: item 2 ("superseded by the uninsured-driver collision deductible waiver terms now in effect") and Total Loss Manual item 2 ("superseded by the new car replacement value basis for surrendered vehicles …"). They name factors whose existence base law already states, and the KB must carry that base law: the Schedule of Deductible Options column "Uninsured-driver collision deductible waiver carried" and the Total Loss Valuation Schedule rows "New car replacement, age limit … / maximum odometer …". They disclose nothing beyond it.
- The rest of the scan is as in revision_1: hops state-derived; no route, chain, tool name or task-mirroring title. Round-1 corpus finding F1 (in the kept-vehicle policy) is closed; see policy_kb/1.md revision_2.
